reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Recording a reflex as absent without reinforcement.
Treating grade 3 as abnormal (it is within the normal range on this scale).
Mixing this scale with scales that use 5 for sustained clonus.
name: Deep Tendon Reflex Grade (NINDS Myotatic Reflex Scale)

version.label: NINDS Myotatic Reflex Scale, 0–4 (Hallett 1993)
version.detail: 0 absent; 1 small or trace, or only with reinforcement; 2 lower half of normal; 3 upper half of normal; 4 enhanced, including clonus if present. Written here as 0–4+ by convention. Other reflex scales (e.g. ones using 5 for sustained clonus) are different versions and are not combined.

purpose: Records the amplitude of a muscle stretch reflex on a standard five-point scale.

calculatorNotice.title: Compare sides
calculatorNotice.message: Grades 2 and 3 are both within the normal range. Asymmetry, and a change from previous examinations, usually matter more than one value.

options.label: Small, less than normal
options.detail: Includes a trace response or one brought out only with reinforcement.

options.label: Lower half of the normal range
Upper half of the normal range
Enhanced, more than normal
options.detail: Includes clonus if present; describe the clonus separately.

inputDefinitions.label: Side
inputDefinitions.help: Added to the copied result; it does not change the grade.

resultStates.label: Absent
resultStates.summary: No reflex obtained, including with reinforcement.
resultStates.detail: Interpret with the other reflexes, strength and sensation; isolated absent ankle reflexes can occur in older adults.

resultStates.label: Reduced
resultStates.summary: Reflex smaller than normal, or present only with reinforcement.

resultStates.label: Within the normal range
resultStates.summary: Reflex within the normal range (grades 2 and 3) at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: A normal-range reflex can still be abnormal if it differs clearly from the other side.

resultStates.label: Enhanced
resultStates.summary: Reflex more than normal, which may include clonus.
resultStates.detail: Look for other upper motor neuron signs: tone, spread, clonus and the plantar response.

clinicalContext.text: Describes the amplitude of one stretch reflex at one examination.
The pattern across reflexes and sides helps separate upper from lower motor neuron and root lesions.

clinicalInsights.text: If clonus is present, record whether it is sustained with the Clonus record in this section.
Use reinforcement (e.g. clenching the teeth or Jendrassik manoeuvre) before recording a reflex as absent.

limitations.text: Subjective, with moderate inter-rater agreement, particularly between adjacent grades.

limitations: Normal reflex amplitude varies between people.
Does not record spread, latency or pendular quality.

confounders.effect: Ankle reflexes may be reduced or absent in older adults.
Some drugs and metabolic disturbances change reflex amplitude.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: The site of the lesion on its own.
Whether a symmetrical brisk reflex is pathological.

guideSections.what: The NINDS Myotatic Reflex Scale grades stretch-reflex amplitude 0–4. Grades 2 and 3 are within the normal range.
guideSections.whenToUse: Every neurological examination of the reflexes, and serial assessment of spinal cord, root and nerve lesions.
guideSections.howToPerform: Relax and position the limb. Strike the tendon with a consistent technique. If no response, use reinforcement. Grade the amplitude and compare both sides.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Interpret with tone, power, sensation, clonus and the plantar response.
